slot.brief: Evaluate a definite integral over [−a, a] whose integrand splits into an odd part (drops) plus a simple even part, using symmetry and a standard result.

verdicts.working: The term x³/(x²+4) is odd, so its symmetric integral is 0. The remaining integral is [½ arctan(x/2)] from −2√3 to 2√3 = π/3.

working:
$\dfrac{x^3}{x^2+4}$ is odd, so its integral over the symmetric interval is $0$. 
$$I=\int_{-2\sqrt{3}}^{2\sqrt{3}}\frac{dx}{x^2+4}=\left[\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{-2\sqrt{3}}^{2\sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}.$$

solution:
Since $\frac{x^3}{x^2+4}$ is odd, its integral over the symmetric interval is zero. Using $\int \frac{dx}{x^2+4}=\frac12\tan^{-1}(x/2)$,
$$I=\left[\frac12\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{-2\sqrt3}^{2\sqrt3}=\frac12\left(\frac\pi3+\frac\pi3\right)=\frac\pi3.$$
